newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's J.Martins sees higher '97 net.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's J.Martins sees higher '97 net.

text.p: Portuguese retailer Estabelecimentos Jeronimo Martins e Filho expects to post an increase in its net consolidated profit of between 20 and 25 percent in 1997, compared with 1996, its Finance Director Jorge Ponce de Leao said.

"We think that the net consolidated profit of Jeronimo Martins could grow by between 20 and 25 percent this year," said Ponce de Leao on the sidelines of a presentation about the company, Portugal's second biggest retailer.
In 1996, Jeronimo Martins registered a net consolidated profit of 11.617 billion escudos.
Ponce de Leao said he expected consolidated sales to rise by around 20 percent to some 430 billion escudos in 1997.
He said he expected the group to invest at least 45 billion escudos in 1997, including investments in its cash-and-carry shops in Poland.

This year Jeronimo Martins invested 15.8 billion escudos in the acquisition of bottled water company Vidago, Melgaco e Pedras Salgadas and two billion escudos in the development of in-store bank Expresso Atlantico.

"We would like to invest 20 billion escudos in the retail and cash-and-carry sectors, but we don't know if it will be possible, as these areas need government and local authority approval," Ponce de Leao said.
